questions.question_text: Vessels A and B contain 60 litres of alcohol and 60 litres of water, respectively. A certain volume is taken out from A and poured into B. After stirring, the same volume is taken out from B and poured into A. If the resultant ratio of alcohol and water in A is 15 : 4, then the volume, in litres, initially taken out from A is
questions.explanation_text:
Vessel A has 60 litres of pure alcohol and Vessel B has 60 litres of pure water.

Let the volume taken out each time be xxx litres.

Since A has only alcohol, the xxx litres taken from A is pure alcohol.

After pouring into B:

Vessel A has (60−x)(60 - x)(60−x) litres of alcohol.

Vessel B has xxx litres of alcohol and 606060 litres of water, totalling (60+x)(60 + x)(60+x) litres.

After stirring B, the mixture is uniform. In every litre of B:

Fraction of alcohol =x60+x= \dfrac{x}{60 + x}=60+xx​

Fraction of water =6060+x= \dfrac{60}{60 + x}=60+x60​

So the xxx litres taken from B contains:

Alcohol =x260+x= \dfrac{x^2}{60+x}=60+xx2​

Water =60x60+x= \dfrac{60x}{60+x}=60+x60x​

After pouring this back into A:

Alcohol in A =(60−x)+x260+x= (60 - x) + \dfrac{x^2}{60+x}=(60−x)+60+xx2​

=(60−x)(60+x)+x260+x= \dfrac{(60-x)(60+x) + x^2}{60+x}=60+x(60−x)(60+x)+x2​

=3600−x2+x260+x= \dfrac{3600 - x^2 + x^2}{60+x}=60+x3600−x2+x2​

=360060+x= \dfrac{3600}{60+x}=60+x3600​

Water in A =60x60+x= \dfrac{60x}{60+x}=60+x60x​

The ratio of alcohol to water in A is given as 15:415 : 415:4.

3600/(60+x)60x/(60+x)=154\dfrac{3600/(60+x)}{60x/(60+x)} = \dfrac{15}{4}60x/(60+x)3600/(60+x)​=415​

The (60+x)(60 + x)(60+x) cancels from numerator and denominator:

360060x=154\dfrac{3600}{60x} = \dfrac{15}{4}60x3600​=415​

60x=154\dfrac{60}{x} = \dfrac{15}{4}x60​=415​

x=60×415x = \dfrac{60 \times 4}{15}x=1560×4​

x=16x = 16x=16

The volume initially taken out from A is 161616 litres.

questions.question_text: For real values of xxx, the range of the function f(x)=2x−32x2+4x−6f(x)=\frac{2x-3}{2x^2+4x-6}f(x)=2x2+4x−62x−3​ is

The denominator can be factored as:

2x2+4x−6=2(x+3)(x−1)2x^2+4x-6 = 2(x+3)(x-1)2x2+4x−6=2(x+3)(x−1)

The function is undefined at x=1x = 1x=1 and x=−3x = -3x=−3.

Let y=f(x)y = f(x)y=f(x) and cross-multiply:

y(2x2+4x−6)=2x−3y(2x^2+4x-6) = 2x-3y(2x2+4x−6)=2x−3

2yx2+(4y−2)x+(3−6y)=02yx^2 + (4y-2)x + (3-6y) = 02yx2+(4y−2)x+(3−6y)=0

For xxx to be real, the discriminant of this quadratic must be ≥0\geq 0≥0.

When y=0y = 0y=0, the equation becomes:

−2x+3=0-2x + 3 = 0−2x+3=0

x=32x = \dfrac{3}{2}x=23​

This is a valid xxx-value (not excluded from the domain), so y=0y = 0y=0 is in the range.

When y≠0y \neq 0y=0, applying the discriminant condition Δ≥0\Delta \geq 0Δ≥0:

Δ=(4y−2)2−4(2y)(3−6y)≥0\Delta = (4y-2)^2 - 4(2y)(3-6y) \geq 0Δ=(4y−2)2−4(2y)(3−6y)≥0

=16y2−16y+4−24y+48y2≥0= 16y^2 - 16y + 4 - 24y + 48y^2 \geq 0=16y2−16y+4−24y+48y2≥0

=64y2−40y+4≥0= 64y^2 - 40y + 4 \geq 0=64y2−40y+4≥0

=4(16y2−10y+1)≥0= 4(16y^2 - 10y + 1) \geq 0=4(16y2−10y+1)≥0

16y2−10y+1≥016y^2 - 10y + 1 \geq 016y2−10y+1≥0

Roots of 16y2−10y+1=016y^2 - 10y + 1 = 016y2−10y+1=0:

y=10±100−6432y = \dfrac{10 \pm \sqrt{100 - 64}}{32}y=3210±100−64​​

=10±632= \dfrac{10 \pm 6}{32}=3210±6​

y=18y = \dfrac{1}{8}y=81​ or y=12y = \dfrac{1}{2}y=21​

Since the coefficient of y2y^2y2 is positive, the parabola opens upward, so the expression is ≥0\geq 0≥0 outside the roots:

y≤18y \leq \dfrac{1}{8}y≤81​ or y≥12y \geq \dfrac{1}{2}y≥21​

Checking whether the excluded points x=1x = 1x=1 and x=−3x = -3x=−3 affect the range:

Substituting x=−3x = -3x=−3 gives 9=09 = 09=0.

Range of f(x)=(−∞, 18]∪[12, ∞)f(x) = \left(-\infty,\, \dfrac{1}{8}\right] \cup \left[\dfrac{1}{2},\, \infty\right)f(x)=(−∞,81​]∪[21​,∞)

questions.question_text: In a school with 1500 students, each student chooses any one of the streams out of science, arts, and commerce, by paying a fee of Rs 1100, Rs 1000, and Rs 800, respectively. The total fee paid by all the students is Rs 15,50,000. From (1)(1)(1):

C=1500−S−AC = 1500 - S - AC=1500−S−A

Substituting in (2)(2)(2):

1100S+1000A+800(1500−S−A)=15500001100S + 1000A + 800(1500 - S - A) = 15500001100S+1000A+800(1500−S−A)=1550000

1100S+1000A+1200000−800S−800A=15500001100S + 1000A + 1200000 - 800S - 800A = 15500001100S+1000A+1200000−800S−800A=1550000

300S+200A=350000300S + 200A = 350000300S+200A=350000

3S+2A=3500⋯(3)3S + 2A = 3500 \quad \cdots (3)3S+2A=3500⋯(3)

From (3)(3)(3):

A=3500−3S2A = \dfrac{3500 - 3S}{2}A=23500−3S​

Since the number of science students is not more than the number of arts students:

S≤AS \leq AS≤A

S≤3500−3S2S \leq \dfrac{3500 - 3S}{2}S≤23500−3S​

2S≤3500−3S2S \leq 3500 - 3S2S≤3500−3S

questions.question_text: For a 4-digit number (greater than 1000), sum of the digits in the thousands, hundreds, and tens places is 15. Sum of the digits in the hundreds, tens, and units places is 16. Also, the digit in the tens place is 6 more than the digit in the units place. questions.explanation_text:
Let the 4-digit number be abcdabcdabcd, where aaa is the thousands digit, bbb is the hundreds digit, ccc is the tens digit, and ddd is the units digit.

From the given conditions:

a+b+c=15a + b + c = 15a+b+c=15 --- (1)

b+c+d=16b + c + d = 16b+c+d=16 --- (2)

c=d+6c = d + 6c=d+6 --- (3)

Since c=d+6c = d + 6c=d+6 and c≤9c \leq 9c≤9, we get d≤3d \leq 3d≤3, so ddd can be 0,1,2,0, 1, 2,0,1,2, or 333.

Substituting c=d+6c = d + 6c=d+6 in Equation (2):

b+(d+6)+d=16b + (d + 6) + d = 16b+(d+6)+d=16

b=10−2db = 10 - 2db=10−2d

Substituting b=10−2db = 10 - 2db=10−2d and c=d+6c = d + 6c=d+6 in Equation (1):

a+(10−2d)+(d+6)=15a + (10 - 2d) + (d + 6) = 15a+(10−2d)+(d+6)=15

a=d−1a = d - 1a=d−1

Testing all possible values of ddd:

ddda=d−1a = d - 1a=d−1b=10−2db = 10 - 2db=10−2dc=d+6c = d + 6c=d+6NumberValid?
0-1106-No, aaa is negative and bbb is not a single digit
10870871No, a=0a = 0a=0 makes it a 3-digit number
21681682Yes
32492493Yes

Since ddd can only range from 0 to 3, the only valid numbers are 168216821682 and 249324932493.

Difference =2493−1682=811= 2493 - 1682 = 811=2493−1682=811

questions.question_text: Teams A, B, and C consist of five, eight, and ten members, respectively, such that every member within a team is equally productive. Working separately, teams A, B, and C can complete a certain job in 40 hours, 50 hours, and 4 hours, respectively. Two members from team A, three members from team B, and one member from team C together start the job, and the member from team C leaves after 23 hours. The number of additional member(s) from team B, that would be required to replace the member from team C, to finish the job in the next one hour, is
questions.explanation_text:
Since every member within a team is equally productive, the per-member rate is found by dividing the team's rate by the number of members:

Member of A =140×5=1200= \dfrac{1}{40 \times 5} = \dfrac{1}{200}=40×51​=2001​ per hour

Member of B =150×8=1400= \dfrac{1}{50 \times 8} = \dfrac{1}{400}=50×81​=4001​ per hour

Member of C =14×10=140= \dfrac{1}{4 \times 10} = \dfrac{1}{40}=4×101​=401​ per hour

Combined rate of 2 members from A, 3 from B, and 1 from C:

=2200+3400+140= \dfrac{2}{200} + \dfrac{3}{400} + \dfrac{1}{40}=2002​+4003​+401​

=4400+3400+10400= \dfrac{4}{400} + \dfrac{3}{400} + \dfrac{10}{400}=4004​+4003​+40010​

=17400= \dfrac{17}{400}=40017​ per hour

Work done in 23 hours =23×17400=391400= 23 \times \dfrac{17}{400} = \dfrac{391}{400}=23×40017​=400391​

Work remaining =1−391400=9400= 1 - \dfrac{391}{400} = \dfrac{9}{400}=1−400391​=4009​

After C leaves, the rate of 2A + 3B:

=2200+3400= \dfrac{2}{200} + \dfrac{3}{400}=2002​+4003​

=4+3400= \dfrac{4 + 3}{400}=4004+3​

=7400= \dfrac{7}{400}=4007​ per hour

Let nnn = number of additional B members needed. Each B member contributes 1400\dfrac{1}{400}4001​ per hour.

To finish 9400\dfrac{9}{400}4009​ work in 1 hour:

7400+n400=9400\dfrac{7}{400} + \dfrac{n}{400} = \dfrac{9}{400}4007​+400n​=4009​

7+n=97 + n = 97+n=9

n=2n = 2n=2

The number of additional members from team B required is 222.

questions.question_text: Rahul starts on his journey at 5 pm at a constant speed so that he reaches his destination at 11 pm the same day. However, on his way, he stops for 20 minutes, and after that, increases his speed by 3 km per hour to reach on time. If he had stopped for 10 minutes more, he would have had to increase his speed by 5 km per hour to reach on time. His initial speed, in km per hour, was
questions.explanation_text:
Total journey time: 5 PM to 11 PM = 6 hours

Let initial speed = vvv km/hr, so total distance = 6v6v6v km

Let ttt = time (in hours) traveled at initial speed before stopping

When Rahul stops for 20 minutes (= 13\frac{1}{3}31​ hour), his new speed becomes (v+3)(v + 3)(v+3) km/hr.

Remaining time after the stop =6−t−13=173−t= 6 - t - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{17}{3} - t=6−t−31​=317​−t

Distance before stop =vt= vt=vt

Distance after stop =6v−vt= 6v - vt=6v−vt

6v−vt=(v+3)(173−t)6v - vt = (v + 3)\left(\frac{17}{3} - t\right)6v−vt=(v+3)(317​−t)

18v−3vt=(v+3)(17−3t)18v - 3vt = (v + 3)(17 - 3t)18v−3vt=(v+3)(17−3t)

18v−3vt=17v−3vt+51−9t18v - 3vt = 17v - 3vt + 51 - 9t18v−3vt=17v−3vt+51−9t

v=51−9t⋯(1)v = 51 - 9t \quad \cdots (1)v=51−9t⋯(1)

When Rahul stops for 30 minutes (= 12\frac{1}{2}21​ hour), his new speed becomes (v+5)(v + 5)(v+5) km/hr.

Note: "10 minutes more" means 20+10=3020 + 10 = 3020+10=30 minutes total, not 10 minutes alone.

Remaining time after the stop =6−t−12=112−t= 6 - t - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{11}{2} - t=6−t−21​=211​−t

6v−vt=(v+5)(112−t)6v - vt = (v + 5)\left(\frac{11}{2} - t\right)6v−vt=(v+5)(211​−t)

12v−2vt=(v+5)(11−2t)12v - 2vt = (v + 5)(11 - 2t)12v−2vt=(v+5)(11−2t)

12v−2vt=11v−2vt+55−10t12v - 2vt = 11v - 2vt + 55 - 10t12v−2vt=11v−2vt+55−10t

v=55−10t⋯(2)v = 55 - 10t \quad \cdots (2)v=55−10t⋯(2)

From (1) and (2):

51−9t=55−10t51 - 9t = 55 - 10t51−9t=55−10t

10t−9t=55−5110t - 9t = 55 - 5110t−9t=55−51

t=4t = 4t=4 hours

v=51−9(4)v = 51 - 9(4)v=51−9(4)

v=51−36v = 51 - 36v=51−36

v=15v = 15v=15 km/hr

Rahul's initial speed was 151515 km/hr.

questions.question_text: The average salary of 5 managers and 25 engineers in a company is 60000 rupees. If each of the managers received 20% salary increase while the salary of the engineers remained unchanged, the average salary of all 30 employees would have increased by 5%. The average salary, in rupees, of the engineers is
questions.explanation_text:
Total salary of all 30 employees:

=30×60,000=18,00,000= 30 \times 60{,}000 = 18{,}00{,}000=30×60,000=18,00,000

The average increased by 5%, and the number of employees is still 30, so the total salary also increased by 5%.

Increase in total salary =5100×18,00,000=90,000= \dfrac{5}{100} \times 18{,}00{,}000 = 90{,}000=1005​×18,00,000=90,000

Engineers' salaries did not change, so the entire 90,000 increase came only from the managers' 20% raise.

20%20\%20% of (Managers' total salary) =90,000= 90{,}000=90,000

Managers' total salary =90,000×10020= 90{,}000 \times \dfrac{100}{20}=90,000×20100​

=4,50,000= 4{,}50{,}000=4,50,000

Engineers' total salary =18,00,000−4,50,000=13,50,000= 18{,}00{,}000 - 4{,}50{,}000 = 13{,}50{,}000=18,00,000−4,50,000=13,50,000

Average salary of engineers =13,50,00025=54,000= \dfrac{13{,}50{,}000}{25} = 54{,}000=2513,50,000​=54,000

The average salary of engineers is Rs. 54,000.

questions.question_text: The monthly sales of a product from January to April were 120, 135, 150 and 165 units, respectively. The cost price of the product was Rs. 240 per unit, and a fixed marked price was used for the product in all the four months. Discounts of 20%, 10% and 5% were given on the marked price per unit in January, February and March, respectively, while no discounts were given in April. If the total profit from January to April was Rs. 138825, then the marked price per unit, in rupees, was
questions.explanation_text:
We're told:
Monthly sales (in units): Jan =120= 120=120, Feb =135= 135=135, Mar =150= 150=150, Apr =165= 165=165
Cost price =Rs. 240= Rs.\ 240=Rs. 240 per unit
Discounts on marked price: Jan =20%= 20\%=20%, Feb =10%= 10\%=10%, Mar =5%= 5\%=5%, Apr =0%= 0\%=0%
Total profit from Jan to Apr =Rs. 138825= Rs.\ 138825=Rs. 138825

We need to find the fixed Marked Price (MP) per unit.

Total units sold =120+135+150+165=570= 120 + 135 + 150 + 165 = 570=120+135+150+165=570

Total Cost =570×240=Rs. 136800= 570 \times 240 = Rs.\ 136800=570×240=Rs. 136800

When a discount is given on the marked price, the selling price per unit becomes MP×(1−Discount%/100)MP \times (1 - \text{Discount\%}/100)MP×(1−Discount%/100). So the revenue from each month is:

Jan: 120×0.80×MP=96 MP120 \times 0.80 \times MP = 96\,MP120×0.80×MP=96MP

Feb: 135×0.90×MP=121.5 MP135 \times 0.90 \times MP = 121.5\,MP135×0.90×MP=121.5MP

Mar: 150×0.95×MP=142.5 MP150 \times 0.95 \times MP = 142.5\,MP150×0.95×MP=142.5MP

Apr: 165×1.00×MP=165 MP165 \times 1.00 \times MP = 165\,MP165×1.00×MP=165MP

Total Revenue =(96+121.5+142.5+165)×MP=525 MP= (96 + 121.5 + 142.5 + 165) \times MP = 525\,MP=(96+121.5+142.5+165)×MP=525MP

Using Profit === Total Revenue −-− Total Cost:

138825=525×MP−136800138825 = 525 \times MP - 136800138825=525×MP−136800

525×MP=138825+136800=275625525 \times MP = 138825 + 136800 = 275625525×MP=138825+136800=275625

MP=275625525MP = \dfrac{275625}{525}MP=525275625​

MP=525MP = 525MP=525

The marked price per unit is Rs. 525Rs.\ 525Rs. 525.

PipeRatio PartsRate (tank/hour)
A4460\dfrac{4}{60}604​
B9960\dfrac{9}{60}609​
C363660\dfrac{36}{60}6036​

Combined Rate=460+960+3660=4960\text{Combined Rate} = \dfrac{4}{60} + \dfrac{9}{60} + \dfrac{36}{60} = \dfrac{49}{60}Combined Rate=604​+609​+6036​=6049​ tank per hour

Time to fill the tank is the reciprocal of the combined rate (since Time =1Rate= \dfrac{1}{\text{Rate}}=Rate1​):

Time=14960=6049\text{Time} = \dfrac{1}{\frac{49}{60}} = \dfrac{60}{49}Time=6049​1​=4960​ hours

Converting to minutes:

6049×60=360049≈73.47\dfrac{60}{49} \times 60 = \dfrac{3600}{49} \approx 73.474960​×60=493600​≈73.47 minutes

≈73 minutes\boxed{\approx 73 \text{ minutes}}≈73 minutes​

12a2=8ah12a^2 = 8ah12a2=8ah

h=3a2h = \dfrac{3a}{2}h=23a​

So the sides are: AB=3aAB = 3aAB=3a, BC=5a2BC = \dfrac{5a}{2}BC=25a​, CD=aCD = aCD=a, DA=3a2DA = \dfrac{3a}{2}DA=23a​

Perimeter =3a+5a2+a+3a2=8a= 3a + \dfrac{5a}{2} + a + \dfrac{3a}{2} = 8a=3a+25a​+a+23a​=8a

Semi-perimeter =4a= 4a=4a

For a tangential polygon, Area=semi-perimeter×r\text{Area} = \text{semi-perimeter} \times rArea=semi-perimeter×r.

Using the trapezium area formula:

Area=12(AB+CD)×h=12(3a+a)×3a2=3a2\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}(AB + CD) \times h = \dfrac{1}{2}(3a + a) \times \dfrac{3a}{2} = 3a^2Area=21​(AB+CD)×h=21​(3a+a)×23a​=3a2

a=4a = 4a=4 cm

The area of the trapezium is 484848 sq. cm.

x+3=(x+1)(x−3)x + 3 = (x+1)(x-3)x+3=(x+1)(x−3)
